title: Denmark plans ban on sharing AI deepfakes without consent
source_used: Euronews (full text); pool item The Daily Star
key_facts: Denmark is due to introduce a bill on Thursday 8 Oct 2026 that would ban sharing realistic deepfakes of people's faces and voices without their consent.
The proposed amendment to Denmark's copyright law would protect ordinary people as well as artists, including against digital imitations of their performances.
The bill would still allow satire, parody and political or social criticism, unless it is misinformation posing serious dangers to others.
The bill follows a broad political agreement reached in June 2025.
Culture minister Zenia Stampe says the main goal is to get tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly.
quote_evidence: "One of the main goals of the bill is to get the tech giants to take down manipulated content quickly, so that it causes the least possible harm."
"With artificial intelligence, you can create manipulated videos and images with just a few clicks and share them on social media," wrote Zenia Stampe, Denmark's culture minister, in a statement.
why_it_matters_hint: People whose faces or voices are copied by AI could get a legal route to stop sharing; the bill is not yet passed.
